title: perf(parser): avoid literal_eval for plain marker strings
head: d17cfaf0b77a5690f03087359e7c8d665a3c728d

families.why: The patch adds a fast‑path in `process_python_str` that returns a `Value` by stripping the surrounding quotes when the string contains no backslashes and consists only of printable characters, avoiding the overhead of `ast.literal_eval`. This avoids the overhead of the AST parser for the common case of simple quoted strings used in environment markers.
families.size_meaning: Micro‑optimisation for a hot parsing path; avoids the heavyweight AST parser for the common case of simple quoted strings in environment markers.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    return [["'cpython'"] for _ in range(min(n, 8))]

families.why: Added a fast‑path in `process_python_str` that avoids `ast.literal_eval` for simple printable string literals without backslashes. Simple environment markers (e.g. `extra == 'linux'`) are common, so skipping the full Python literal parser saves the relatively heavy C‑level parsing overhead for the common case.
Added fast‑path in process_python_str that returns the literal string slice when the string contains no backslashes and is printable, avoiding the slower ast.literal_eval call.

The fast‑path adds an `isprintable()` call and a backslash check for every marker string. For very short marker strings this extra Python‑level check may outweigh the saved `ast.literal_eval` cost, especially on very short strings where the AST parser is already fast.
families.size_meaning: Micro‑overhead per call; measurable only in tight loops parsing many markers.

families.why: For string literals that contain a backslash (e.g. escaped quotes or escape sequences) the fast‑path test `"\\" not in python_str` scans the whole token, then `str.isprintable()` scans it again before falling back to `ast.literal_eval`. This double scan adds overhead for the relatively rare escaped strings.

The fast‑path skips ast.literal_eval for any string without a backslash, but strings containing escaped non‑printable characters (e.g., '\x00') are printable yet not literal strings; the fast‑path would return the literal escaped text instead of the evaluated character, causing incorrect marker evaluation.
